finalText:
**Found it. 10 of 40 tests fail, and every single failure has a percent coupon in it.**

`engine.js` rounds the running total to cents twice on the way — once after the percent coupon, once after the flat one. The contract says round once, at the very end, in the cart's own currency. That early rounding throws away up to half a cent, and then the exchange rate multiplies the loss.

Flat coupons alone never fail, because taking `$5` off a cent-exact total is still cent-exact. Only the percent step leaves a leftover fraction to lose.

`USD` and `EUR` pass here by luck of the two test baskets, not because they are safe. Across a sweep of prices from `$5` to `$200`, `EUR` is off on about 10% of carts, `CAD` 17%, `JPY` 18%.

Removing both intermediate `round(...)` calls in `computeTotal` matches the contract on all 682,535 combinations I swept.

One more thing worth a look: a cart can go negative today. `$5.05` with `SAVE10PCT` and `FLAT5` returns `-0.45`.
